commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[levanter] Count full-attention layers explicitly in lm_flops_per_token (#9633)

Count the 26-layer Snowball model's seven full-attention layers in the
shared `lm_flops_per_token` estimate. The harness previously counted
six, as noted in #9613, because the June trainer used a private
estimator with an explicit layer-count argument. The long-layer
schedule, every fourth layer plus the last, was also specified in three
places.

`lm_flops_per_token` now accepts `num_full_attention_layers`, which
takes precedence over the `global_every` stride. The June trainer and
Snowball synthetic harness use the shared helper, and the private
estimator is deleted. For the Snowball shape, the shared helper matches
the deleted function exactly at 4096 and 65536 tokens. The Snowball
model exposes `long_attention_layer_mask` for its scan and
`num_long_attention_layers` for the harness; the June trainer counts
layers with its model's existing schedule function. A test confirms that
the harness and June trainer calculate the same FLOPs per example for
that shape.

The corrected estimate raises the harness's measured MFU by 0.4% at a
4096-token context. The harness docstring's undercount note is removed.

Part of #9462

---

<details>
<summary>Verification: how the numbers were checked</summary>

All comparisons are exact float equality, not tolerances.

1. **Deleted June helper against the shared helper.** The private
`_lm_flops_per_token` from the pre-change
`experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/train.py` and the shared
`lm_flops_per_token` with `num_full_attention_layers=7` were called with
the Snowball shape (hidden 2560, intermediate 1280, shared 2560, 26
layers, 20 heads, 5 KV heads, 256 experts, top-4, window 2048, vocab
128256). Results: 5,305,917,440 FLOPs per token at 4096 tokens and
9,735,741,440 at 65536 tokens from both functions. The old stride path
(`global_every=4`, six full layers) gives 5,284,823,040 and
9,081,815,040, the 0.4% and 7% undercounts.

2. **June trainer before and after.** `_compute_flops` from the
pre-change module and from this branch were run on 36 configurations:
layer counts 1 through 12, 24 through 28 and 64, each at the June
default shape and at the Snowball shape. FLOPs per example and
full-attention layer counts matched in all 36, which also confirms that
summing the model's schedule mask equals the arithmetic formula it
replaced.

3. **Harness against the June trainer.**
`experiments/grug/snowball_synthetic/test_flops.py` builds a June config
from the Snowball shape and asserts both estimators give the same FLOPs
per example and seven full layers. It runs in CI.

4. **Model behaviour.** `lib/levanter/tests/test_snowball.py` (14 tests,
excluding slow, checkpoint and HF cases) passes with the scan using
`long_attention_layer_mask`, and the harness tiny preset trains on CPU.

To reproduce item 1 on this branch:

```bash
uv run python -c "
from levanter.utils.flop_utils import lm_flops_per_token as f
kw = dict(hidden_dim=2560, intermediate_dim=1280, num_layers=26, num_kv_heads=5, num_heads=20, vocab_size=128256, glu=True, num_experts=256, num_shared_experts=1, num_experts_per_tok=4, shared_intermediate_dim=2560, sliding_window=2048)
for s in (4096, 65536): print(s, f(**kw, seq_len=s, num_full_attention_layers=7), f(**kw, seq_len=s, global_every=4))"
# 4096 5305917440.0 5284823040.0
# 65536 9735741440.0 9081815040.0
```

</details>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Curate task sources with Zephyr artifacts (#9642)

Add an artifact pipeline that converts pinned task datasets into audited
and filtered TaskSpec Parquet files. Library family modules provide
normalization, source-specific quality rubrics and grader checks as a
`TaskPipeline`. Experiment bindings select pinned sources and downloads,
pair them with a policy in a `DatasetRecipe`, and construct the artifact
graph. Every selected input remains in the audit, including rejected
tasks, reasons, model findings, checks and cleanup lineage.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[Experiment binding: source pins and download inputs] --> D[Download pinned source files to object storage]
    R[Library TaskPipeline: normalizer, rubric, checks] --> A
    D --> S[Read staged files: reshard 1, limit N, reshard 64]
    R --> N[Normalize records into TaskSpec]
    S --> N
    N --> A[Audit: grader controls and GLM quality review]
    Q[(FineStore: exact request and model revision)] <--> A
    A --> P[Audit Parquet: inputs, tasks, checks, review evidence]
    P --> F[Filter: final keep or reject with reasons]
    F --> W[Optional selected-task repair with a separate rubric]
    W --> V[Recheck, review and filter repaired candidates]
    F -->|Repair disabled| C[Concatenate one final artifact per source]
    V --> C
    C --> M[Canonicalize: deduplicate, reject reference conflicts, prioritize eval]
    M --> O[Parquet views: audit, accepted, train, eval, executable]
```

Each source follows the same graph for bounded and full runs. The limit
is applied after download with
`reshard(1).take_per_shard(N).reshard(64)`; changing it reuses
downloads. Zephyr owns row processing, shard reuse, serialization and
reductions. FineStore caches schema-valid GLM completions by exact
request and model revision across catalog versions. An unfinished mapper
can resubmit an in-flight remote batch; attempt-specific evidence is
retained. Family and stage revisions, TaskSpec schema version and the
repair prompt digest scope artifact invalidation.

Filtering makes a final quality decision independently of grader
readiness. Unbound evaluators are excluded from the executable view.
When repair produces a candidate, it replaces the parent's row in that
source's final artifact, receives fresh checks and review, and retains
the original audit in its lineage. Rows without a replacement pass
through. Canonical merging retains audit rows and records exclusion
decisions; accepted views omit exact-contract duplicates and conflicting
typed references and give evaluation records priority over matching
training records. Private inputs remain part of duplicate identity for
opaque source evaluators.

Family normalizers emit private grader packages using VerifyIT's
existing specifications and execution contract. Standard math, numeric,
MCQ, schema and constraint tasks select reusable modes. Source-specific
ARC parsing, avoided-action rules, calendar postconditions and reference
gates are recipe-owned scripts bundled with their configuration. A
script may use VerifyIT components or implement its own scoring; adding
one requires no TaskCompendium registration.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[Family normalizer] --> T[TaskSpec public task]
    R --> P[Private grader package]
    P --> S[Standard VerifyIT spec and fixtures]
    P --> C[ScriptSpec plus grader.py and config.json]
    S --> V[VerifyIT grading contract]
    C --> V
    E[Extracted answer or captured evidence] --> V
    V --> O[Scored, invalid-task or infrastructure verdict]
    O --> A[Pipeline controls and grader readiness]
```

TaskCompendium extracts submission evidence and stages private files.
Answer-file graders run through VerifyIT; coding graders use a fresh
network-disabled machine with a pinned private image. Controls run the
same emitted package. Grader scripts and fixture bytes participate in
task identity and GLM review evidence. Opaque script contracts
deduplicate only when their full private semantics match; distinct
private script contracts do not establish conflicting typed answer keys.
Incidental preference metadata remains in the raw audit.

Unbound evaluators preserve their source contract and return an unscored
infrastructure verdict. Reasoning Gym remains unbound until an isolated
runtime is supplied because its upstream scorers may execute candidate
expressions. Private tests are hidden from the solving environment, but
submitted code can still read them within the grading machine. TaskSpec
uses upstream role-grouped resources and named tool-provider
requirements; its optional episode prototype retains interaction-tool
declarations and capture paths, which direct chat rejects.

The [source
catalog](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/let-s-mock-up-a-clean-verify-fil/experiments/post_training/task_curation/atlas_catalog.json)
accounts for 196 Atlas listings: 148 mapped, 45 explicitly excluded and
three KTO contributor selectors without recoverable membership metadata.
The registry exposes 150 source names, including two additional sources.
A full-corpus release remains outstanding. Legacy TaskTrove converters
follow main.

Nemotron Ultra selections are grouped by family in the experiment. Each
group binds a library policy explicitly, including math placeholder
inputs and repository membership inputs where required. Direct-source
and archive bindings use the same separation. Adding a source does not
require a new execution path.

The [pipeline
reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/let-s-mock-up-a-clean-verify-fil/docs/references/task-curation.md)
describes recipe definitions, artifact flow, caching and execution.

commits.author: himanshk96
commits.message:
[dedup] Send connected-components labels only from changed nodes (#9773)

Send a node's component label to its neighbors only in the iteration
after
the label decreased, and carry only the key, the self flag and the
component
id in that message. Each Hash-to-Min iteration re-sent every node's
label to
every neighbor and packed the record id, an empty adjacency list and the
other
node fields into messages whose reducer reads only the component id.
Labels
only decrease and a node re-sends whenever its label drops, so a
neighbor
already holds a label no larger than anything an unchanged node would
re-send.
Every `it_N` row, the per-iteration change counts and the convergence
round
are unchanged; the self-message still carries the full node and is
always
sent, so resume and the fuzzy-dedup consumer see the same files.

On a synthetic 285k-node graph with 26 bands per node that converges in
six
iterations under the local client with eight reduce shards:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iteration stages, wall | 166 s | 76 s |
| messages per iteration from the third on | 4.64M | 0.29M |
| scatter payload per iteration from the third on | 1,131 MiB | 232 MiB
|
| scatter payload, first iteration | 1,131 MiB | 778 MiB |
| peak RSS, whole run | 9.0 GiB | 7.6 GiB |

Final labels are identical. Old and new also agree on 3,000 random
graphs
with shuffled message arrival (paths, stars, cycles, self-linked
singletons,
iteration caps from 1 to n+3, resume from every intermediate iteration)
and on
a differential matrix over chains, stars and dense graphs with
`preserve_singletons` on and off, one and four reduce shards, converged
and
capped runs, and resume from a capped run. The dedup suite passes
unchanged.

[codehealth] Catch consumer policy in shared libraries (#9754)

# Agentic-lint catalog refinement

Add `ml-consumer-policy-in-shared-layer` for code that places one
consumer's UI or deployment choice in a reusable library. Require a
visible owner boundary and suppress generic shared APIs. Also grant the
workbench writer DELETE on the existing admin-owned lint findings table
when that table exists, so a refreshed telemetry sync can replace
findings.

## Evidence

- The fixed sync covered 2026-09-05 17:23 UTC to 2026-10-05 17:23 UTC.
The post-sync rolling 30-day `list-prs --human` query returned 1,801
human events across 320 pull requests. Three placement comments on three
distinct PRs support the new rule: [Zephyr-only UI in Iris,
#9088](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9088#discussion_r3992072039),
[a production applet URL in Zephyr,
#9173](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9173#discussion_r4076493379),
and [dataset-specific graders in a shared package,
#9642](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9642#discussion_r4169325356).
The #9642 comment has no source anchor, so it is corroborating human
feedback, not a probe case.
- These PRs have 9 recorded `review-pr` invocations and 12 generic
findings: #9088 has 3 invocations and 0 findings; #9173 has 3 and 3;
#9642 has 3 and 9. A #9173 bug finding also identified a deployment URL
problem, so that feedback was partly surfaced in production. The new
rule has no production exposure yet. The nearest existing import rule,
`ml-reverse-layer-import`, had 0 findings in 500 current-catalog
eligible successful runs; the #9088 code has no reverse import.
- [A shared Zephyr plan representation,
#9173](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9173#discussion_r4076540419)
is an allowed case. [Protocol decoding discussed in
#9220](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9220#discussion_r4138276633)
lacks a clear owner boundary in the available source window and is a
suppression case.

## Probe results

The provisional catalog identity is
`0764a93a0030f5002f7ec411faf4b6f5e1d24e11f1315fd2013a38c3155274ab`; the
new rule identity is
`41b813bef715797851f6ff3df4109e496b824432abba79e64fa66fa3fb5e645f`. Each

These are experiments on selected historical contexts, not a production

## Validation

- `tests/codehealth/test_refinement_workbench.py`: 15 passed.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and Pyrefly: passed; the affected-test
selector selected 0 package tests for the infra-only diff.

on attempt 2 after the grant, persisting 320 pull requests and 1,511

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Reduce duplicate work when loading Finelog dashboards (#9734)

Training charts load from their metric query without waiting for
seven-day attempt history or Iris execution-health queries. Attempt
history uses one ordered aggregate, and results of identical source
queries are shared for 20 seconds with a 128 MiB Arrow cache cap. Shared
dashboard panels use explicit point budgets so panels with different
widths use the same query interval for the same window. The Training run
picker refreshes on dashboard load.

Finelog snapshots only namespaces referenced by a query, using
DataFusion's table-reference resolver so joins, subqueries, and CTEs
keep working. Require `async-trait` 0.1.92 to remove redundant generated
`#[must_use]` attributes rejected by Rust 1.99 Clippy.

On 11 copied immutable production segments (4.26 million rows, 60.5 MB),
the Training metric query's median warm execution time fell from 325 ms
to 141 ms; metrics plus attempt history scanned 9.32 MB instead of 13.06
MB. These are local debug-build measurements, not a production dashboard
latency forecast. A 31-namespace fixture reduced SELECT 1 latency from
14–15 ms to 5 ms by avoiding unrelated snapshots.

No live dashboard, hub configuration, or storage layout was changed.
[Incident and benchmark details](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/603).

commits.message:
[hero] Keep two completion jobs active (#9745)

The hourly hero-completions workflow now keeps up to two sampling jobs
active in its default `next` mode, not one.

One sample set takes about 40 hours from submission to result, mostly
the queue wait for 64 GB200 GPUs at batch priority. The hero writes a
permanent checkpoint about every 28 hours. With one active job the
backlog grows, and the newest-first order never gets to the older
checkpoints: steps 156000 to 180000 have no attempts, while 186000 and
192000 completed.

After merge, one manual `submission=all` run clears the current backlog.

commits.message:
[iris] Forward task preemption to the execution peer (#9720)

Forward task preempt and fail requests for federated jobs to the
controller running their tasks. The hub previously acknowledged
overrides against mirrored tasks without stopping the peer runtime,
leaving a hung trainer running.

Resolve descendant jobs and attempt qualifiers on the execution peer,
and restrict forwarded actions to jobs handed off by the requesting
cluster.

[Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/599).
